findings.title: Layout shift above the 0.1 budget on /
findings.description: Lab CLS 0.169 at 320 px over load, a full scroll and one click (budget ≤ 0.1). The largest shift moved #opening (0.169). Lab values from one local run on this machine; they vary between runs and are not field data. FUN-08 (LCP, INP) is advisory and never fails the gate.

ground_truth.description: The slots for a day arrive about a second after the page opens or a day is chosen, and nothing says they are on their way: the grid is empty, the status line is blank, and Next is enabled. Pressing Next during that time does nothing at all. A resident who taps a day and then Next, as people do, sees no slots and no response, and may try another day or give up.

When the slots arrive, about a second after the page opens, the empty grid grows by several hundred pixels and everything under it (the Next button, the opening days, the footer) jumps down the page with no input from the resident: a layout shift of well over the 0.1 budget on every width, measured in the lab. A link to #opening from another page lands on the wrong place for the same reason: the slots arrive after the browser has scrolled to the anchor.

The 'Few left' tag on a slot is amber text on an amber tint whose values the script computes at run time from the council's hue: about 3.0:1 in the light theme and 3.2:1 in the dark theme for 16 px bold text, below the 4.5:1 that text of that size needs. The stylesheet holds no colour literal, so the failure exists only on a rendered page. The tag is the one thing that tells a resident a slot is about to go.

At 360 px and below the script sizes the slot grid's three columns from the window's width instead of the page's content box, so the grid runs 14 to 15 px past the right edge and the page scrolls sideways; the last column's slots and their tags are cut at the edge. From 361 px up the stylesheet's own grid applies and nothing overflows.

The slot buttons show no focus at all: a style the script injects at run time removes their outline (meant for the pressed look), and nothing replaces it. Every other control on the page keeps the 3 px focus ring. A keyboard user tabbing through 29 slots cannot see which one they are on.

Today's slots that have already started, or start within half an hour, are shown as free and can be chosen (today is Monday 12 October at 10:05, so 08:00 to 10:20 are offered). The refusal comes three steps later, after the details are typed and Book is pressed: 'The 10:20 slot today can no longer be booked. Choose another slot or day.' with no link back to the slots.

That a van, or a car with a trailer, needs a permit is said only behind an icon-only info button. Choosing 'Van' reveals the permit field 1.2 seconds later, under the fold on a phone, with nothing drawing the eye to it, and Next accepts an empty permit. The rule is enforced on the confirm page ('A van needs a permit number'), which has no permit field; the resident has to work out that 'Change vehicle' is the way back.

A chosen slot is held for five minutes and no page shows the hold or its end. When it has lapsed, Book waits 1.5 seconds and then says 'This slot is no longer available.' while the summary's slot line changes to a dash: the slot is dropped from the booking without saying that the hold ran out, and the only way to another slot is 'Change slot', which forgets the day.

'Book this slot' stays enabled while the booking is made (1.5 seconds) and shows no progress: no busy state, no label change. A second press in that time turns the press into 'cancel': the done page still shows a reference, is titled 'Booked' and says 'Show this at the gate', with a small status line saying the booking is cancelled and not on the gate's list. A resident who taps twice, as people do when nothing seems to happen, arrives at the gate with a cancelled booking.

The script moves every 'Few left' slot to the front of the grid at run time (a CSS order it sets per button), so the grid reads 08:20, 09:00, 09:40, 12:00 before 08:00. The document, Tab and a screen reader keep the chronological order, so focus jumps around the visible grid and the morning and afternoon headings no longer sit above their slots.

The line that says how many slots a day has ('20 slots free on Saturday 17 October') is written into a plain paragraph and only then given aria-live, so a screen reader is never told the slots have arrived or how many there are; the next change would be announced, but the day's count is the one that matters.

'Change slot' on the confirm page opens the first step on today's date with no slot chosen, whatever day the resident had picked: the day and the slot are forgotten (the vehicle, the waste and the typed details are kept, and Next returns to the confirm page). Nothing says so; a resident who only wanted the afternoon of the same day has to find the day again.

A slot button shows only its start time. That a slot lasts 20 minutes, when it ends and that the resident must arrive within it are only in the button's tooltip, which appears on hover and never on a phone. The intro says '20-minute slot' once, above the fold.

The done page gives the reference and what to bring, but not the day, the slot or the vehicle that were booked. A resident who books on Monday for Saturday has nothing to check the time against on Saturday morning except memory, and the gate turns away a vehicle that does not match the booking.

material.reply:
The booking flow is not ready for launch as handed over. The worst problem: a resident can end up with a booking the gate will reject while the page in front of them says "Booked". There are also a few accessibility failures that hit phone and keyboard users on the very first screen.

I reviewed it at phone widths (320 and 375 px) and desktop widths, in light and dark mode. Several independent reviewers checked it, then other reviewers confirmed or rejected each problem and rated how severe it is without seeing who found it. All of this is expert review. Nothing has been tried with residents yet.

## What to fix first

1. **A double tap on "Book this slot" cancels the booking.** While the booking is processing (about 1.5 s), a second tap silently changes the button to "Cancel booking". The booking is then saved as cancelled. The resident still lands on a page headed **"Booked"** with a reference, and only a small red line says it isn't on the gate's list. That page also still says "Show this at the gate". Double taps are common on phones, so this sends people with a loaded car to a gate that turns them away. All three raters gave it the top severity. The fix:
   - ignore repeat taps and show "Booking…" while it processes;
   - head the cancelled page "Booking cancelled", and change its tab title too;
   - remove the gate instructions from the cancelled page.
2. **"Few left" slots are moved out of time order.** Every slot with "Few left" is pulled into an unlabelled block above "Morning", so 13:40 sits among the morning times. Residents may think 08:00 or 09:20 are gone. The keyboard and screen-reader order also jumps backwards (WCAG 1.3.1, 1.3.2 and 2.4.3). Nearly every reviewer found this independently. It comes from one CSS rule (`order:-1`).
3. **Slot buttons show no keyboard focus.** A rule added at run time removes the focus outline (WCAG 2.4.7).
4. **The "Few left" label is hard to read.** It measured 3.0:1 contrast in light mode, against the 4.5:1 required. In dark mode the code works out to about 3.4:1; that figure was calculated, not measured. Either way it's below the minimum in the theme many residents use.
5. **The slot grid doesn't fit a small phone.** At 320 px the page scrolls sideways (WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow).

## Next round, also high priority

- **Permits are checked too late.** A van with no permit, or a wrong one, gets through the vehicle step and is only stopped after "Book this slot". The error there doesn't link back to the field. The permit field also shows for cars, and the permit rule is hidden behind an (i) button.
- **The 5-minute hold is invisible.** Nothing says a slot is held or for how long. When it expires, the message gives no next step and "Book this slot" stays the main button.
- **The confirmation page leaves out the booking itself.** It doesn't repeat the day, the time window or the vehicle, which is what someone glancing at their phone at the gate needs.
- **"Change slot" resets the day to Today.** Someone moving their Saturday booking can quietly end up booking Monday.
- **Today's earlier slots look bookable.** They show as free and are refused only at the last step.
- **No online way to change or cancel.** Residents can only do it by phone, on weekdays.
- **Screen readers aren't told when slots load.** "22 slots free…" isn't announced, and the slot area is blank for about a second with no loading message.

## Worth keeping

- The dark theme holds together well on a phone apart from the "Few left" label.
- Slot buttons are large tap targets, and full slots say "Full" in text rather than relying on colour.
- The centre's rules are written plainly on the first page.
- The reference is shown large.

## Where things stand

The UI-Evaluator check reached no assurance level against the L3 target in your product notes. It is held back by the WCAG failures above and the two top-severity problems.

Some things can't be checked by machine and need a person:
- VoiceOver and TalkBack in dark mode;
- real 200% zoom;
- typing with an IME (one finding about this is waiting on that test).

The "how distinctive and appealing is it" checks for minified code didn't run, and the design reviewers called the look plain and generic for a council form. That's a lower priority than the problems above.

Because the agency's files are minified and you have no original source, each fix means either editing the bundle or asking the agency. Most of the top items are small changes.

## Files

All in `.ui-evaluator/runs/20261016-125610-audit-standard/`:
- `report.md` and `report.html`: the full report;
- `debrief.md`: the review summary;
- `agree-disagree.csv`: a sheet for you or the agency to mark findings agree or disagree.

2. Is online change and cancel in scope for launch, or is the phone line the intended route?
3. Should the "Few left" marker stay at all, or is "Full" enough?
